questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to draw a family tree
How accurate DNA tests for tracing your ancestry are
Why people emigrated to the United States
How DNA is passed from parents to children
questions.why: They discuss how accurate DNA ancestry tracing is.

questions.q: What did Beth's mum find out about their family?
options: Many of their ancestors had emigrated to the US
Their family came from Ireland
They had a famous ancestor with the same name from 1700
They had relatives all over Europe
questions.why: Beth says her mum found a lot of their ancestors had emigrated to the United States.

questions.q: Why is it easy for Neil's family to trace their ancestors?
options: They have kept old family letters
They took a DNA test
Neil has an unusual surname
They have always lived in the same town
questions.why: Neil says he's lucky to have an unusual surname, so it's quite easy to trace his ancestors.

questions.q: Why did listener Chris call the programme?
options: His results showed that he had some famous relatives in the United States
His test kit never arrived
He wanted to sell his DNA results
His results mostly matched, but a few small errors made him doubt them
questions.why: He says results were broadly in line with expectations but had 'some little glitches'.

questions.q: According to genealogist Louise Baldock, what is the difference between 'ancestry' and 'ethnicity'?
options: They mean exactly the same thing
Ancestry is about places, and ethnicity is about people
Ancestry is about your recent family, and ethnicity is about older family
Ancestry is about real people; ethnicity is about where they came from
questions.why: She says ancestry is about your actual forebears, while ethnicity is thought of in geographical terms.

questions.q: What did presenter Greg Foot's first DNA test show?
options: That his family was mostly Irish
That he had no European ancestors at all, which was a big surprise to him
That his family had come from England for five generations, as he knew
That the test had failed
questions.why: The first company's results matched what he knew: the past five generations came from England.

questions.q: What was surprising about Greg's second DNA test?
options: It showed no evidence of English ancestry at all
It said he was 99.9% English
It said he came from Asia
It gave exactly the same results as the first company's test
questions.why: It showed north and west Europe and Irish, Scottish and Welsh – 'explicitly not English'.

questions.q: According to Neil, why were Greg's two results so different?
options: Greg sent the wrong samples
The companies compare DNA with different databases
His DNA had changed in the time between the two different tests
One company made up the results
questions.why: Neil says companies use different databases, so it's not surprising the results were different.
